item.dc:creator: Tyler Brooks
item.description: Electric vehicles will probably never fully replace the internal combustion sports car , but mainstream daily drivers are living on borrowed time . It's not like anyone with no idea which wheels are powered or how many cylinders their car has cares about a missing exhaust note.
item.content:encoded:
Briefing: Electric vehicles will probably never fully replace the internal combustion sports car , but mainstream daily drivers are living on borrowed time . It's not like anyone with no idea which wheels are powered or how many cylinders their car has cares about a missing exhaust note.

Electric vehicles will probably never fully replace the internal combustion sports car , but mainstream daily drivers are living on borrowed time . It's not like anyone with no idea which wheels are powered or how many cylinders their car has cares about a missing exhaust note. But while EVs are taking off in the rest of the world , the U.S. lags behind, thanks in large part to pro-oil propaganda . People believe all sorts of myths about EVs, and I'm sorry, but short test drives won't fix it. Which means EV owners need to start acting like they have an obligation to lend friends and family their cars.

A few days in an EV won't change anyone's mind if their lifestyle doesn't match what EVs currently offer, and that's fine. But if they've been tricked by a bunch of pro-oil myths, you may find that a few days with your car is all it takes to convince them that EVs are the best thing ever. Because even an hour-long test drive doesn't show you the benefits of living with a gas station in your garage. It's the kind of thing that probably requires a three-day loan at a minimum, because they have to see how it fits into their regular lives.

While their plans include new renewable energy and storage, they continue to spend on fossil fuels, building new gas, and in the case of APS, extending coal use. Instead of facilitating a timely transition to affordable, clean energy, both utilities — and especially APS — continue an expensive dependence on fossil fuels that keep ratepayers in a dangerous cycle, paying the price for decades.

Arizonans already experience some of the highest electric bills in the country, with some of the most planned gas in the country. Yet, instead of easing energy burden and saving its customers millions of dollars, APS prolongs costly coal operations at the Four Corners coal plant, worsening climate impacts, increasing air pollution, and threatening public health.

On a dry hillside in Chamwino, central Tanzania, mango farmers used to watch their trees struggle through the long months without rain. Irrigation was technically possible: A diesel pump could lift water from a nearby borehole. But in practice, fuel was too expensive and too unpredictable for smallholders to run the system often enough. When diesel prices rose, farmers irrigated less, production dropped, and most households stayed locked into low-yield farming and razor-thin margins.

When new, the Geo Metro convertible was fabled to have 55 horsepower and 58 pound-feet of torque, but Kohrmann was smart enough to dyno test his remarkably clean 1992 Metro convertible before setting off on his cross-continental journey. Before that, though, he gave it a tune-up and fixed the air conditioning — or at least he thought he did... After a 50-second pull, the dyno showed the Metro made 43 horsepower and 53 lb-ft of torque. That's more than enough to complete a 2,838-mile road trip that includes a 10,000-foot climb, right?

There's never a guarantee a startup car company will actually make it. Automotive history is littered with companies that never made it more than a few years, and after some of Rivian's early financial troubles, it wasn't out of the question that the Irvine, California-based company could join that group. Well, following the introduction of the R2 , those fears seem to be all but squashed.

Rivian just posted its third-quarter results for 2026, and the compact-crossover-sized R2 helped raise the automaker's deliveries by 46% year-over-year to 19,248 vehicles, according to Car and Driver . That means Rivian is increasing its yearly sales projection to between 67,000 and 70,000 vehicles — up from 65,000 to 70,000. It also just so happened to outsell the larger and more expensive R1S and R1T flagships combined, as well as the EDV delivery van. I should note that Rivian didn't explicitly say how many R2s it sold, though. This news comes even though the only R2 that Rivian currently sells is the most expensive Performance version of the electric SUV, and the idea that Rivian is still "early in the ramp" of R2 production, according to CEO RJ Scaringe, who spoke with Reuters .
